title: No document says how to start a campaign on an application that does not exist yet
foundBy: session agent, from a fresh-agent test: an agent given only the binary designed a new-application campaign and named a repository path that was never going to exist
details:
Nothing tells an operator what to do when the application does not exist yet.

The product handles the case well. A repository path that is absent plans as an empty repository, with a deterministic initial commit pinned and `initialize` set, and planning creates nothing. An unborn git repository is adopted on main. A directory that holds files and is not a repository is refused rather than adopted in silence.

Proved by probe. Running plan with `--repo` pointed at an absent path exits 0 and leaves the parent directory empty. The pinned initial commit is derived rather than read, so every host computes the same one.

No document a reader can reach says any of it. MANUAL names no initial commit and no adoption rule. PLAYBOOK describes a repository as a writable clone at the campaign's base commit and never covers the case where there is nothing to clone. SPEC R123 requires the behaviour, and it is written as a rule for the implementation rather than as guidance for an operator.

The cost showed up in a test. An agent given only the binary was asked to design a campaign building a new task-tracking application. It read the playbook and then wrote a placeholder repository path into its profile. Nothing it could reach told it what the tool does with a path that is not there.

Building something new is one of the strongest reasons to run a campaign, so this is a path an operator meets early.
